text: The blade stays where the hand holds it, while the shavings curl away and fall. Kenaz is the steady edge that takes wood down to the shape waiting inside it. What comes off is not waste, it is simply what the form did not need. Something in your work may now be clear enough that you cannot unsee it.

The blade holds its line while the shavings curl away and fall. Kenaz works like that hand at the wood, taking off what hides the shape beneath. Something in your making has grown clearer, Kuky, by what you have cut from it. This may be a time when you can see the form you are after, and cannot unsee it.

The needles keep moving, though the yarn thins toward its end in your hand. Nauthiz is the work continued with less than the work asks for. You are counting stitches now, not rows, and the pattern narrows to what the last of it can hold. Something here runs short, and you have stopped pretending otherwise.

The needles keep going, though the ball has shrunk to a few turns of thread. Your hands know the pattern and carry on, counting what is left with each stitch. Nauthiz is the work that continues while the supply runs thin, and the measuring that starts on its own. Somewhere in your life there is a need you have been knitting around rather than naming.

The wool, the long evenings, the counted rows — and then only the sweater, finished in your hands. Jera is the slow turn from work into something you can wear. What you hold now took a whole winter, and most of that winter you could not see it. Something in your life has come due, Kuky, from a choice you made before you knew its shape.

The sweater lies finished across your knees, months of evenings gathered into one weight of wool. Jera is the slow turn that brings a thing back to your hands in another form. The stitches you no longer remember making are holding the shoulders now. Something in your life may be arriving whole, built from work you did before you knew its shape.
